title: Egress & DNS Guardian: Terraform module for VPC security controls, upgrades, and health checks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Build a composable Terraform module (egress-dns-guardian) that standardizes Redwood Private VPC security controls: managed Security Groups, NACLs, private Route53 zones/resolvers, and configurable egress ACLs/policy templates. The module must support safe upgrades (schema migrations), automated health checks, idempotent apply semantics, and integration points for audit logging and Canary rollouts.

Goals:
- Provide a single opinionated module that teams can include in Private stacks to enforce outbound policies and private DNS resolution presets.
- Ship migration helpers so existing customers can move from ad-hoc egress rules to module-managed policies with zero or minimal disruption.
- Expose observability: terraform output hooks for console ingestion, health check resources, and drift detection notes.
- Support multi-account and multi-AZ deployments with region-aware resolver endpoints.

Scope / Features:
- Security group templates generated from service tags (service_tag -> allowed CIDR/ports mapping).
- NACL orchestration for subnet-level hardening (deny-by-default templates with explicit allow lists).
- Private DNS: Route53 private hosted zone creation + optional conditional forwarding to customer resolvers; automated VPC association management.
- Egress policies: policy layers (default, restricted, monitored) with ability to map workloads to layers via tags.
- Upgrade path: a migration plan implemented as Terraform scripts + terragrunt examples that perform staged rule replacement and reconciliation.
- Health checks: Lambda-backed periodic validators (or native cloudwatch metrics) that verify connectivity to allowed egress endpoints, DNS resolution tests, and surface failures as Terraform outputs and CloudWatch alarms.
- CI tests: terratest suite + mock resolver tests (using LocalStack in CI) and a plan-only policy guard that fails PRs on non-idempotent changes.
- Audit hooks: emit change metadata to a central S3 bucket (or Kinesis) in structured JSON for Console to ingest.

Non-goals:
- Not responsible for application-level firewalling (WAF) or per-packet inspection.
- No vendor lock to a single cloud provider; initial implementation targets AWS only.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module published to internal Terraform registry with versioning and CHANGELOG.
- Migration docs and example stack in Redwood-examples repo.
- Automated terratest CI covering create/update/destroy and an upgrade path demo.
- Health check Lambda + CW alarms deployed by module optionally and documented.
- Security review signed off and release notes prepared for private-2026.04.

Implementation plan:
1) Design (this ticket): finalize resource boundaries, variables, and outputs.
2) Prototype: minimal module that creates security groups, NACLs, and private zone and runs basic terratest. (Est 1 week)
3) Migration helpers + staged replacement tooling (Est 1 week)
4) Health-checks + observability outputs (Est 3 days)
5) CI + terratest + LocalStack integration (Est 4 days)
6) Docs, examples, security review, and release.

Risks & Tradeoffs:
- Tight coupling vs flexibility: making module too prescriptive could slow adoption. We mitigate by supporting policy layers and opt-outs.
- Zero-downtime migration complexity: staged rule replacements can temporarily increase rule counts and risk transient failures; mitigation: test harness and canary rollout scripts.
- Lambda health checks add operational burden; make them optional and pluggable.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Egress+and+DNS+Guardian+Design (draft)
- Example repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/egress-dns-guardian (prototype branch)
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/487 (initial module skeleton)
- Terratest: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tests/pull/92

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize variable naming and outputs. Miguel to open initial PR for module skeleton (blocking: terratest infra updated).
- Security to schedule initial design review next Wed.

Owner notes:
- Aim for backwards-compatible variable names; any breaking rename should be a major release and documented in migration guide.
- Provide sample policy templates for common SaaS endpoints and internal service patterns.
